newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila SEC sets conditions on futures exchange.
newsitem.headline: Manila SEC sets conditions on futures exchange.

text.p: The Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission said it had set three conditions to be met within a month before the Manila International Futures Exchange (MIFE) can resume operations.
In an order signed last week but released on Monday, SEC Chairman Perfecto Yasay said there should be at least ten licensed commodity futures brokers in order to make MIFE's operations viable.
The MIFE's clearing house should either be a bank or a reputable auditing firm independent of the MIFE and acceptable to the Commission, the SEC said.
The SEC said any opening and closing of clients' accounts should be approved by the Commission.
The SEC issued on June 23 a cease and desist order on MIFE and six of its brokerage houses following reports of widespread irregularity in the exchnage.
It has since lifted the suspension order against the MIFE and directed it to reform the market.
The suspension orders on three of six brokers was also revoked but the others remain under investigation.
The MIFE offered future contracts in copra, dry cocoon, soybeans, coffee and major currencies, but trading volumes were negligible.
